tasks.summary: I fixed the reviewer finding. mp-data had withheld the `dataset export` summary because it matched a corpus string. The summary line now holds only totals and fixed messages, as in the contract's example: tables, rows, omitted_columns, skipped_tables, cycles_broken, self_references, unknown_columns, plus differences under --check. Table names, column names, `rows:<table>` keys and per-table sha256s no longer go in it. They now go to stderr, which mp-data keeps in the data-zone log. That covers each table's name, row count, sha256 and columns, any cycle-broken table names, and under --check the names of files that differ. The summary messages now give counts, for example 'N files differ' and 'load order: N cycles broken'. With the corpus present (604 strings), both data-plane export calls now exit 0 and are no longer withheld. Northwind result: 28 tables, 611 rows, 2 omitted columns, 0 cycles broken, 1 self reference, 0 unknown columns, and --check found 0 differences. The guard passes on both repos. I updated the tests to check the counts-only summary (no table or column names in the line) and that the per-table detail is on stderr. I also updated docs/formats/dataset.md to match.
notes: Summary change: the dataset export summary line no longer contains table or column names, `rows:<table>` keys or per-table sha256s, because dataplane.corpus_hit matches substrings. That detail goes to stderr (the mp-data log in the data zone) and is still in dataset.json. A consumer that needs per-table counts reads them from dataset.json or the log inside mp-data, not from the summary.

This makes the S0.dataset build spec line 'Summary: per-table row counts, sha256s and column names' unsafe through mp-data. The contract's example summary (counts tables and rows only) already fits the new behaviour, so docs/contracts.md needs no change.

Other commands whose summaries list design names (for example per-table count keys) can be withheld the same way once a corpus exists. Owners of later tasks may want to keep names out of the mp-data summary lines as well.

tasks.summary: I fixed the reviewer finding. strings.txt now leaves out a data string that matches design text anywhere, not only an exact table or column name. That covers a substring of a longer object, table or column name, the engagement's own id, client, db_name, paths and source path, and a fixed list of summary fields, count keys and message fragments. mp-data checks summaries for any corpus string as a substring, so these strings no longer make it withhold a summary. The rebuilt Northwind corpus has 214 code files, 27 data files and 597 strings (604 before). After the rebuild, `mp-data --slot s0_guard_fix1 dataset export ... --check` exits 0 and reports 0 differences, where the reviewer's run exited 2 with 'summary withheld'. I added a synthetic fixture row whose data value sits inside a form name, plus two tests. One checks the new exclusion rule directly. The other runs the real parse, dataset export and export --check on the synthetic engagement, then guard, and confirms with mp-data's own corpus_hit that neither export summary is withheld. All six acceptance commands exit 0.
notes: Fix: build_corpus in toolkit/guard.py now uses _inside_design_text to leave a string out of strings.txt when it occurs inside any design name, the engagement's id, client, db_name, paths or source path, or SUMMARY_VOCABULARY (the quiet summary fields, the dataset and guard count keys, and fixed message fragments). Before, it only removed strings that exactly equalled a name.

Extra check, not an acceptance command: after guard rebuilt the corpus, `mp-data --slot s0_guard_fix1 dataset export /home/cloudcli/sourcecode/modernization-pipeline/engagements/northwind-demo/engagement.json --out /home/cloudcli/engagements/northwind-demo/private/datasets/engagement --check` exited 0 with differences 0, tables 28 and rows 611. It is no longer withheld.

Upstream S0.dataset fix round 1 had already changed toolkit/commands/dataset.py: per-table names now go to stderr and the summary keeps aggregate counts only. The guard-side exclusion is a second layer of defence. The new test runs the real export summary against the rebuilt corpus through dataplane.corpus_hit.

Remaining limit: a data string could still match text that spans JSON punctuation, or an ad hoc message from another command that is not in SUMMARY_VOCABULARY. If another command's summary is withheld later, add its fixed text to SUMMARY_VOCABULARY.
The fixture tblTrays.txt gained one synthetic row whose note value sits inside a form name. It is hand-written greenhouse content, not client material.

issues.problem: xml_row_elements drops any row element that has no child elements (`len(el) == 0`). Access XML exports leave NULL fields out, so a row whose columns are all NULL (possible in a table with no required key) would vanish from iter_rows without a warning or count. The dataset's row count would then be lower than the source's, with no sign of it. The old code did the same, and it does not affect Northwind, where every table has a key.
